purpose: Follow the pressure, not the sound label
researchReuse: Read the sealed report and claim ledger for scope, version, evidence and limits; no fresh scientific or code experiment.
readingContext: Offline desktop and 390/320px mobile; both languages and keyboard controls.

composition.question: Two paths, one listening position
composition.relationship: Incoming noise and the loudspeaker output travel different acoustic paths. The controller must account for what reaches the ear, not merely flip the sign of the outside microphone signal.

composition.question: A small timing error matters more at higher frequency
composition.relationship: For an assumed uncompensated error of 0.10 ms, the phase error is 3.6° at 100 Hz and 36° at 1,000 Hz. This is a single-tone calculation, not a headphone measurement or universal frequency cutoff.

composition.question: The seal blocks a path; ANC adds pressure
composition.relationship: Passive isolation changes how sound enters. Active control adds another pressure wave. Switching ANC off leaves the physical barrier in place; taking the headphones off changes both.

composition.question: Partly reduced can still mean audible
composition.relationship: Speech spans many frequency components. Some may be reduced while others remain. Recognizable residual speech does not prove that no speech was attenuated, or that its pressure was amplified.

composition.question: Fit and mode can change the comparison
composition.relationship: A seal leak changes the acoustic path. Transparency deliberately admits outside sound; adaptive modes can change behavior. Keep fit and sound source fixed when comparing ANC on and off. That is a proposed comparison, not a test performed here.
